subject: what truecap actually is
preheader: a fast rental screen built around standard investment metrics and editable assumptions.
headline: TrueCap is the rental underwriter I wished existed when I was buying deals.
body: Most rental analysis tools fall into two camps. Either they're glorified rent calculators that ignore taxes, insurance, vacancy, and PM fees. Or they're 47-tab spreadsheets that take half an hour and still get DSCR wrong because the formula was copied from a forum in 2014.

TrueCap is the middle path. Paste a U.S. address and review cap rate, cash-on-cash, DSCR, NOI, an operating-expense breakdown, selected-rule fit, and a secondary Screening Index. It uses standard formulas and labeled, editable starting assumptions. The index is triage context, not a probability, appraisal, or investment advice. Your lender may calculate DSCR or expenses differently, so verify the inputs and program rules before relying on the result.

The philosophy is simple: faster first-pass screening leaves more time for due diligence on the opportunities that deserve it. TrueCap helps you decide what to inspect more deeply; it does not replace that inspection.

Free includes unlimited first-pass analyses, up to 5 saved deals, and no card requirement. Pro adds editing and unlimited saves, a target-dependent Offer Ceiling, sensitivity, BRRRR and flip models, 10-year projections, illustrative tax impact, modeled exits, comparison, and PDF decision reports. The pricing page is the source of truth for current plan details.
If you've never tried it, pick the next listing in your inbox and paste the address. In about 60 seconds, you can decide whether it deserves deeper review.
